title: Git: branches, cleanup & releases
intro: Merging, undoing, cleaning up and tagging releases.

blocks.h: Switch to the branch you want to merge into
blocks.p:
Branches let you work on new features separately from the main branch (main or master). When a feature is ready, you merge it.

git checkout branch_name switches to the branch.

Suppose your feature branch is called feature-login.

git merge combines the changes from the branch you specify into the current branch.

If there are conflicts, Git will tell you, and you’ll need to resolve them manually in the affected files.
-d deletes a branch that has been merged.
If the file is already listed in .gitignore but Git is still tracking changes locally, that means the file was tracked before it was added to .gitignore. This is expected Git behavior.
blocks.code:
git rm --cached <file>
git commit -m "Stop tracking a file"

blocks.h: Keep the remote file (discard local changes)
blocks.p:
Git is protecting your local changes from being overwritten.

Use this if your local changes are not needed and you want your local to be the same with remote.

This deletes:
Untracked files
Untracked directories
Now your working tree matches the remote checkout byte-for-byte.
Use this if your .gitignore edits are intentional. If conflicts appear after stash pop, Git will prompt you to resolve them.
blocks.code:
git stash push -m "Local .gitignore changes"
git pull
git stash pop

blocks.p:
GitHub Actions will automatically:
- Build executables for macOS, Linux, Windows
- Create a release at https://github.com/username/repo-name/releases/tag/v1.0.0
- Attach all binaries to that release
blocks.code:
# Make sure you're on main and it's up to date
git checkout main
git pull origin main

# Create and push a version tag
git tag v1.0.0
git push origin v1.0.0

blocks.p:
git push origin :v1.0.1
is shorthand for
git push origin :refs/tags/v1.0.1
blocks.code:
git tag -d v1.0.1          # delete local tag
git push origin :v1.0.1    # delete remote tag
git tag v1.0.1             # recreate the tag
git push origin v1.0.1     # trigger new build

blocks.p:
This undoes the change but keeps history clean.

Find the commit hash if you don’t know it:
git log --oneline
blocks.code:
git checkout main
git revert <commit-hash>
git push

blocks.h: Full flow: pull → work → commit → merge → push
blocks.code:
git checkout main
git pull origin main      # 1. Sync with GitHub

git checkout -b feature-x # 2. Create feature branch
# work on code

git add .
git commit -m "Add feature X"

git checkout main
git pull origin main      # 3. Re-sync before merge
git merge feature-x       # 4. Merge locally

git push origin main      # 5. Push merged code
